title: Many Circuits, One Mechanism: Input Variation and Evaluation Granularity in Circuit Discovery
abstract: arXiv:2606.06267v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Circuit discovery methods identify subgraphs that explain model behaviors, and structural differences between discovered circuits are commonly interpreted as evidence of distinct mechanisms. We test this assumption by varying input-token frequency while holding the task fixed. The discovered circuits appear specialized by frequency when compared structurally, but functional and representational analyses show no reliable evidence of corresponding differences. We term this mismatch phantom specialization. Using the Literal Sequence Copying task across four frequency bands plus a frequency-weighted control, we extract 75 circuits from five Pythia models (70M-1.4B). translated_title: 多电路，单一机制：电路发现中的输入变化与评估粒度
translated_abstract: 电路发现方法识别出解释模型行为的子图，而发现电路之间的结构差异通常被解释为不同机制的证据。我们通过固定任务并改变输入令牌频率来检验这一假设。结构上比较时，发现的电路似乎按频率特化，但功能性和表征性分析未显示相应差异的可靠证据。我们将这种不匹配称为“幻影特化”。使用字面序列复制任务，涵盖四个频率区间及一个频率加权控制，我们从五个Pythia模型（70M-1.4B）中提取了75个电路。我们发现结构不同的电路实现相同的计算：特定频带的边在频带间广泛转移，大多数频带共享的核心在70M以上模型中恢复至少99%的电路性能，因果交换干预确认了这一现象。
tldr: 该研究发现，电路发现中结构差异可能不代表机制差异，而是输入频率变化导致的“幻影特化”，实际功能上共享单一计算机制。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that structural differences in circuit discovery may not reflect mechanistic differences, but rather "phantom specialization" from input frequency variation, with functionally shared single computation.
